title: Name the bank's settlement files

blocks.text: The nightly settlement job uploads one payment file per run to the bank, and the bank's gateway files each upload under the date and time in its name. The bank's specification:

The date is the cut-off's calendar date, year, month and day; the time is on the 24-hour clock, to the minute. The gateway refuses a file dated in the future and overwrites a file that has the name of an earlier one.
Finish `stamp(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/SettlementFiles.java`, so the job names every run correctly, on every day of the year. About two lines.

cases.says: a morning run is named after its date and its time to the minute
seconds and fractions of the cut-off do not appear in the name
a run in the last days of December is named with its own calendar year, not the next
an afternoon cut-off is written on the 24-hour clock
the month is written where the month goes and the minute where the minute goes

origin.section: Pattern Letters Are Case-Sensitive, and YYYY Is the Year of the Week

concepts: Pattern letters are case-sensitive: MM is the month and mm the minute, HH the 24-hour hour and hh the 12-hour one that needs a.

YYYY is the week-based year, whose weeks come from the formatter's locale, so it prints the next year in the last days of December (or the previous one in the first days of January); the calendar year is uuuu or yyyy.
